2. Abdul Gafur, predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners as plaintiff, filed the aforesaid suit for perpetual injunction restraining the defendant opposite parties from entering into 21 decimals of land of RS plot No. 229 and from cutting their khayer trees standing thereon on the allegations that their predecessor Abdul Gafur Mondal and his brother Abdul Wahed Mondal purchased share of suit holding by kabala dated 20.7.43; that the RS record having been wrongly prepared in the name of defendant No. 1 and others dispute arose over the possession of the said kabala land and, as such, the said Abdul Gafur and his brother Abdul Wahed brought Title Suit No. 113 of 1950 in the Court of the Munsif, Goalanda against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and some others and the suit was decreed on compromise with defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in terms of solenama; that accordingly 2 annas share of plaintiff and his brother and 6 annas share of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in the suit jote was admitted; that Abdul Wahed sold his share to Abdul Gafur by registered kabala dated 30.5.60; that after compromise decree in the said suit plaintiffs exclusively possessed the suit land by amicable partition and planted khayer trees, jack fruit trees and raina trees, etc. in the said land and the defendants did not possess the suit land since then; that on 1.7.79 defendants having threatened the plaintiff with dispossession he was compelled to file the suit. Plaintiff having died during pendency of the suit the petitioners is substituted as his heirs. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1-5 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations stating, inter alia, that Afaz Mondal, Akbar Mondal, Khanaz Mondal and Chhanuddin Mondal predecessor-in-interest of the contesting defendants Nos. t to 5 purchased the suit land along with other lands by kabala dated 14.5.40 and also obtained settlement by patta dated 27.8.40 from the original owners and have been in possession of the suit land and their names were recorded correctly in the RS Khatian. Their further case is that Chhanuddin Mondal possessed 10 decimals of land of the suit plot and the plaintiff possessed 11 decimals of land of the suit plot. The suit plot being contiguous to the homestead of Chhanuddin Mondal and the said 11 decimals of land of the plaintiffs being required for the purpose of his pathway for ingress and egress to the main road from his house Chhanuddin Mondal got the said 11 decimals of land by way of exchange of his 10 decimals of land of plot No. 83 and since then the said Chhanuddin Mondal and after his death the defendants are in possession of the suit land by using part of the same as their pathway and the remaining part by cultivation and having also grown different kinds of trees by the side of the pathway; that the plaintiff having no title and possession in the suit land out of grudge to misappropriate the khayer trees, the plaintiff filed the suit; that the defendants were not aware of any compromise decree or ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 113 of 1950 and at that time defendant No. 1 was a minor and other defendants were female and, as such, decree is fraudulent and not binding upon the defendants.
